facts.text: Orion Descent Stage was deployed at Descartes Highlands during Apollo 16 in 1972.
Lower half of Lunar Module Orion. Young and Duke explored the Descartes highlands — a region geologists hoped was volcanic but turned out to be impact breccia.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.

Landing in the highlands tested geological predictions about lunar volcanism — the crew's samples disproved the volcanic hypothesis, showing the terrain was formed entirely by massive asteroid impacts.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Descartes Highlands.
Remains at Descartes; its ascent stage developed a guidance malfunction after separation and tumbled onto the Moon in an uncontrolled impact.
